completion.text: {"adjudications":[{"id":"F1","decision":"confirmed","reason":"In the source, 'neither of them' refers to Darwin and Tennyson, through the Palgrave comparison. The revision drops Palgrave and Tennyson, so the phrase now means Darwin and Sir Charles. That makes the text say Lyell never came to town, which contradicts both 'the Lyells were intimate at the Legation' and Lyell's later call at the Legation. The fix keeps the source's point that Darwin never met Adams.","evidence":[{"document":"017.source","paragraph":1,"quote":"Sir Charles constantly said of Darwin, what Palgrave\nsaid of Tennyson, that the first time he came to town, Adams should be\nasked to meet him, but neither of them ever came to town"},{"document":"017.revision","paragraph":1,"quote":"but neither of them ever came to town, or ever cared to meet a young American."},{"document":"017.revision","paragraph":3,"quote":"when Sir Charles came to the Legation to inquire about getting his \"Principles\" noticed in America"}]}],"replacements":[{"old":"but neither of them ever came to town, or ever cared to meet a young American.","new":"but Darwin never came to town, or ever cared to meet a young American.","reason":"Removes the false implication that Lyell never came to town while keeping the source's point that Darwin never met Adams. This is a minimal local edit with a net change of -1 word.","finding_ids":["F1"]}],"remaining_concerns":[]}
